newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish forestry shares seen gaining more.
newsitem.headline: Swedish forestry shares seen gaining more.

text.p: Despite Swedish forestry shares surging 17 percent on the Stockholm Stock Exchange in the past month, there is room from further gains when the economy picks up speed, analysts said on Wednesday.

The recent upturn, which outperformed a 6.9 percent gain in the exchange's general index, was mainly fuelled by a stronger dollar but could also be partly attributed to expectations for an upturn in the economy.
"To some extent, players have discounted a coming economic upturn but definitely not all of it," Erik Magnusson, analyst at Nordbanken, told Reuters.
In theory there was potential for forestry shares to rise roughly 20-30 percent, Magnusson said.
"The required return has fallen from around 17 percent to 13 percent because of the current low interest rate levels," Magnusson said.

"This would indicate that share prices at the next profit peak would be around 20-30 percent higher compared to peak years 1989 and 1995. I don't, however, think that company profits will reach 1995 levels, as this was an extreme year."
He added that this example was based on current interest rate levels, but said there was a risk that rates would rise when the economy picked up.
Furthermore, Magnusson cautioned that the forestry sector swings so sharply that it was always difficult to make estimates about potential share price peaks.
Other analysts also saw investors turning to forestry shares.

"We are in a reassessment phase now, where you also get help from the dollar...there are some signs indicating a coming pick up, better volumes and thicker order books," Mikael Jafs, analyst at Swedbank, said.
"The key issue is where the dollar will land, if it will remain at current levels in the future or not."
But some analysts warned of exaggerating the dollar's impact on the forestry sector.
"The dollar dependance is not that big, at least not transaction wise where the mark and the franc are more important," said Lars Kellberg, analyst at Enskilda Securities.
"But a strong dollar could have dynamic effects and trigger an uppick in European economic trends."
Kellberg said, however, that Swedish shares have performed much stronger than their U.S. counterparts, which could be the effect of the stronger dollar.
On Wednesday, the forestry sector was up 0.51 percent at 1315 GMT, while the exchange's general index was up 0.16 percent at 2,702.27.
Stora was 0.5 crown higher at 106.5, while AssiDoman rose 1.5 to 200, MoDo gained four to 247 and SCA advanced one to 169 crowns.
